description_short: Exploring the miraculous birth stories of the Buddha alongside the most important marvel: his moment-to-moment awareness of arising and passing phenomena.
description_long:
In this inspiring talk, Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta (MN 123), where Venerable Ānanda recounts the wonderful and marvellous qualities of the Buddha. The discourse begins with monks discussing the Buddha's supernatural knowledge of past Buddhas, then moves through the miraculous events surrounding the Bodhisattva's descent from Tusita heaven, his conception, birth, and first moments of life.

Bhante contextualizes these mythic elements within the axial age — a time when new forms of consciousness were emerging across cultures, from Lao Tzu in China to Socrates in Greece. However, he emphasizes that the Buddha's most remarkable quality isn't the supernatural phenomena, but his constant moment-to-moment awareness: "feelings are known as they arise, as they are present, as they disappear."

This teaching beautifully bridges the devotional and practical aspects of Buddhism, showing how the Buddha himself brought the discussion back to ground level — the foundation of vipassanā practice. Perfect for understanding how mythic narrative and direct experience work together in the Theravāda tradition.
